title: Cocartesian recognition from represented mixed mapping spaces
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, standard simplices, mapping spaces and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations, fibres and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and mapping-space composition of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Let $p:E\to\Delta^1$ be an inner fibration of small quasicategories and put $C=E\times_{\Delta^1}\{0\}$ and $D=E\times_{\Delta^1}\{1\}$. For $x\in C$ and $y\in D$, write $\operatorname{Map}^{01}_E(x,y)$ for the homotopy fibre over the unique edge $0\to1$ of the induced map on mapping spaces.

Suppose that for every $x\in C$ a vertex $T_x\in D$ and equivalences of spaces
$$\epsilon_{x,y}:\operatorname{Map}^{01}_E(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_D(T_x,y)$$
are given, coherently natural in $y\in D$. Naturality includes compatibility with postcomposition by all arrows of $D$ and its higher simplices; no functor $C\to D$ is assumed in this hypothesis.

Then $p$ is a cocartesian fibration. For every edge $e:x\to y$ over $0\to1$, the edge $e$ is $p$-cocartesian if and only if the component represented by $\epsilon_{x,y}(e)$ is an equivalence in $D$. In particular, an edge corresponding to the identity of $T_x$ is a cocartesian lift of $0\to1$ with target $T_x$, up to the specified mapping-space identification. No nonemptiness or limit or colimit hypothesis on either fibre is imposed.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 2.4.4.3 (opposite-category dual), printed p. 131 in the cited edition: homotopy-pullback mapping criterion. The represented mixed-mapping specialization and inverse test are expanded by the agent; they isolate the recognition argument in former step 4 of the item, following Higher Algebra Lemma 4.2.2.20 and Remark 4.2.2.21. Read online; WANTED: archived HTT in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical criterion.

proof.text: The fibers $C,D$ are quasicategories: an inner horn in either fiber is an inner-horn problem for $p$ over the constant simplex at $0$ or $1$, and its lift stays in that fiber. A right-pinched mapping simplex in $\Delta^1=N([1])$ is a monotone map $[n+1]\to[1]$ with its first $n+1$ vertices fixed at the source. Consequently its mapping spaces from $0$ to $0$, $0$ to $1$, and $1$ to $1$ are exactly $\Delta^0$, and from $1$ to $0$ it is empty. If both endpoints of a mapping simplex in $E$ are in one fiber, its base simplex is constant; thus the right-pinched mapping space agrees degreewise with the mapping space in that fiber. There are no mapping simplices from $D$ to $C$. For $x\in C,z\in D$ the map on mapping spaces has target $\Delta^0$, whose path space is also $\Delta^0$. The defined homotopy fiber therefore identifies with the whole mapping space: put $M_x(z)=\operatorname{Map}^{01}_E(x,z)=\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)$. These identifications preserve restriction of simplices and postcomposition by arrows in $D$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, interval specialization; explicit degreewise calculation from the mapping-space and fiber definitions.

proof.text:
Fix an edge $e:x\to y$ over $0\to1$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to this same inner fibration $p$ between quasicategories. For a test vertex $z\in C$, the square has empty upper-left and lower-left corners, lower-right corner $\Delta^0$, and upper-right corner $\operatorname{Map}_C(x,z)$. Its path-space homotopy pullback is empty, so this test always holds. For $z\in D$, both bottom corners and their path space are $\Delta^0$, so the path-space pullback is precisely $M_x(z)$. The upper-left corner is $\operatorname{Map}_D(y,z)$ by Step 1, and the comparison map is precomposition with $e$. Thus the criterion gives
$$e\text{ is }p\text{-cocartesian}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{for every }z\in D,\ e^*:\operatorname{Map}_D(y,z)\longrightarrow M_x(z)\text{ is a weak equivalence}.$$
There are no other vertex colors to test. In particular this use of the criterion does not presuppose the existence of any cocartesian lift.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, opposite-category dual, pp. 131–132; base mapping spaces calculated in Step 1.

proof.text:
Write $a$ for an edge of $D$ representing the component $\epsilon_{x,y}(e)\in\operatorname{Map}_D(T_x,y)$. Such a representative exists by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. The hypothesis is coherent naturality in $y$, so for the entire parameter space of arrows $g:y\to z$ it supplies
$$\epsilon_{x,z}(g\circ e)\simeq g\circ\epsilon_{x,y}(e).$$
This is a homotopy of maps with domain $\operatorname{Map}_D(y,z)$, with its higher parameter simplices retained. Since precomposition and postcomposition are restrictions of the canonical composition class, the displayed homotopy says
$$\epsilon_{x,z}\circ e^*\simeq a^*:\operatorname{Map}_D(y,z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_D(T_x,z).$$
Replacing the point $\epsilon_{x,y}(e)$ by its representative $a$ does not change that composition class. Each $\epsilon_{x,z}$ is an equivalence. Composing with it and using the displayed homotopy therefore shows that $e^*$ is an equivalence exactly when $a^*$ is. This is just two-out-of-three for the induced maps on components and based homotopy groups (the homotopy identifies them with the usual change of basepoint). No Yoneda theorem or functor $C\to D$ is used.

source.place: Represented specialization of Proposition 2.4.4.3: unpacking the stated coherent naturality hypothesis, with the canonical composition classes.

proof.text: Suppose $a:T_x\to y$ is an equivalence. Choose an inverse edge $b:y\to T_x$ with both inverse-triangle witnesses. Associativity, units and component dependence in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] give homotopies $b^*a^*\simeq\mathrm{id}$ on $\operatorname{Map}_D(y,z)$ and $a^*b^*\simeq\mathrm{id}$ on $\operatorname{Map}_D(T_x,z)$, for every $z\in D$. Here $b^*:\operatorname{Map}_D(T_x,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_D(y,z)$ is precomposition by $b$. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] to these two maps and homotopies. Hence every $a^*$ is a weak equivalence, including when the mapping spaces are empty. Steps 2–3 imply that $e$ is $p$-cocartesian.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, represented specialization; inverse-edge implication written using associativity and the two inverse equations.

proof.text:
Conversely suppose $e$ is $p$-cocartesian. Steps 2–3 say that $a^*$ is a weak equivalence for every $z\in D$, hence bijective on components. Work in $hD$ from [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. At $z=T_x$, surjectivity gives an edge $b:y\to T_x$ with $[b][a]=1_{T_x}$. At $z=y$, injectivity gives $[a][b]=1_y$, because
$$([a][b])[a]=[a]([b][a])=[a]=1_y[a].$$
Thus $[a]$ is invertible. The invertible-component criterion in the cited node supplies the two inverse-triangle witnesses, so $a$ is an equivalence edge of $D$. This proves the required recognition in both directions. The argument is the two-object inverse calculation, not a further lemma hidden in an appeal to Yoneda.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, represented specialization; explicit inverse test in the homotopy category.

proof.text: For each $x\in C$, the equivalence $\epsilon_{x,T_x}$ is surjective on components. Choose a component of $M_x(T_x)$ mapping to the component of $\mathrm{id}_{T_x}$; by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] it has an edge representative $\lambda_x:x\to T_x$ in $E$. Its image under $p$ is the unique $0\to1$ edge, and Step 1 identifies its component in $M_x(T_x)$ with that representative without extra base-path data. The represented component is the identity component, hence an equivalence by the same invertible-component criterion. Steps 4–5 make $\lambda_x$ $p$-cocartesian. This proves existence with the stated target $T_x$, not merely a target equivalent to it. The statement's wording up to the mapping-space identification records exactly the chosen component.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, represented specialization; existence obtained from the identity component of each representing object.

proof.text: Every degenerate edge in $E$ is $p$-cocartesian by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. The only edges of $\Delta^1$ are $\mathrm{id}_0$, $0\to1$ and $\mathrm{id}_1$. For either identity choose the degenerate edge at the specified source. For $0\to1$ and a specified source $x$ over $0$, use $\lambda_x$ from Step 6. These are all source-and-base-edge pairs, so the inner fibration $p$ is a cocartesian fibration by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. If $C$ is empty there are no mixed lifting requirements; if $C$ is nonempty the assumed vertices $T_x$ already force $D$ nonempty. If $D$ is empty the hypothesis therefore forces $C$ empty as well. Nothing in this proof invokes limits, colimits, or additional nonemptiness assumptions.

source.place: Definition 2.4.2.1, opposite dual, and Corollary 2.4.1.6, opposite dual: cocartesian lifts of all interval edges.

lean.statement: theorem mixed_mapping_cocartesian_recognition (E : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory E] (p : E ⟶ Δ[1]) (_hp : InnerFibration p) (R : MixedMappingRepresentation p) : cocartesianFibrationOver p ∧ (∀ (x : (fiber p (stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv.symm 0)) _⦋0⦌) (s : (mixedMappingFamily p x) _⦋0⦌), IsCocartesianEdge p (Functor.natTransEquiv ((unitHomEquiv _).symm s.1.2)) ↔ IsEquivalenceEdge (fiber p (stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv.symm 1)) (SSet.yonedaEquiv (Functor.natTransEquiv ((unitHomEquiv _).symm ((R.equivalence x).app _ s).1.2)))) ∧ (∀ x : (fiber p (stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv.symm 0)) _⦋0⦌, ∃ (s : (fiber (mixedMappingProjection p x) (R.target x)) _⦋0⦌) (i : (fiber (representedMixedProjection p (R.target x)) (R.target x)) _⦋0⦌), ((pullback.snd _ (representedMixedProjection p (R.target x))).app _ i).1.2 = diagramVertex (SSet.const (X := Δ[1]) (R.target x)) ∧ SSet.mapπ₀ (R.fiberMap x (R.target x)) (π₀.mk s) = π₀.mk i ∧ IsCocartesianEdge p (Functor.natTransEquiv ((unitHomEquiv _).symm ((pullback.snd _ (mixedMappingProjection p x)).app _ s).1.2)))
lean.note: The specified coherent epsilon is presented as an equivalence over the whole target fiber between the existing comma left-fibration models. Canonical pinch equivalences identify the fibers with the stipulated right-pinched mapping spaces; over the interval the mixed homotopy fiber is the whole mapping space. Recognition uses the actual image of each mixed edge. The identity-component equation is in the fiber over the exact representing vertex. The two added, already landed statement dependencies own the reused comma projection and canonical fiber map; no notion is redeclared and no statement correction is needed.
